channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Beijing brought China's first local standard for green packaging by catering and takeaway businesses into force on 1 September, dividing meal packaging into simple and sealed categories and discouraging plastic film sealing where it is not needed.
item.description:
The guidelines were issued by the Beijing Municipal Market Supervision Administration and took effect on 1 September. They separate packaging into two categories. For sealed packaging, plastic cling film should not be used for room-temperature, chilled or frozen items unless necessary, and only a small amount of narrow-edge film should be used where high-temperature meals require sealing; for beverages, easy-to-separate sealing paper is recommended according to temperature. For simple packaging the guidance is item-specific: bags for steamed buns and pancakes, fewer packaging layers for burgers, sandwiches and hot dogs, paper boxes for pizza and cake, lidded but unsealed containers for stir-fries and rice bowls, aluminium foil with a sealing bag for barbecue, biodegradable materials for fried foods, and compartmentalised packaging for dumplings and sushi. Reporting describes the intent as encouraging degradable materials and eliminating the practice of boxes within boxes. This is a municipal standard rather than a national one, and the reporting available does not indicate whether it is mandatory or advisory.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Food-service packaging is an adhesive technologies application through carton and box construction, sealing films, labels and laminates, so a standard that pushes away from plastic film sealing and toward paper and biodegradable substrates changes which bonding systems are specified. Two points temper the immediate significance: it applies to Beijing rather than nationally, and reporting does not establish whether compliance is compulsory. Against that, a specification written down to the level of individual meal types gives converters an unusually clear target, though the reporting does not indicate whether the standard is likely to be adopted beyond Beijing. Points that may be worth considering include whether adhesive systems for paper-based and biodegradable food packaging are qualified for the substrates this standard favours, and whether Chinese converter customers are signalling reformulation ahead of any wider adoption.

China Economic Net | Beijing Daily | China Economic Net

item.title: The German furniture association VDM reported first-half turnover of EUR 7.7 billion, down 2.7% year-on-year, with upholstered furniture down 10%; it says manufacturers have lost about a fifth of their sales over four years.
item.description:
Within the total, kitchen furniture revenue rose 1% while other categories declined, upholstered furniture most steeply at 10%. Order intake shows the same split: kitchen orders were 0.9% higher in the first half than a year earlier, upholstered orders 10.5% lower. Business on the German domestic market was the weakest part, down 4.1%. Jan Kurth of the VDM pointed to rising material, energy and wage costs, a weak consumer climate, purchasing power shifting toward travel and leisure, stagnating housing construction and increasing international competitive pressure. The four-year decline of about a fifth is more striking than the half-year figure because, as the reporting notes, it has occurred while furniture prices rose — Kurth assumes manufacturers added certainly ten to 15 percent in production price increases in recent years, meaning volumes have fallen further than revenue.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Furniture manufacturing is a direct consumer of wood adhesives, edge-banding adhesives, laminating systems and coatings, so a volume decline of this depth in Germany's furniture sector reduces demand for a specific and identifiable product group rather than for the portfolio generally. The divergence within the sector is usable: kitchens are holding while upholstery falls sharply, and those use different adhesive systems. Kurth's observation that the four-year revenue decline of about a fifth occurred while production prices rose by something like ten to 15 percent implies the underlying volume decline over that period is considerably larger than a fifth, which matters more for adhesive consumption than the revenue figure does, since adhesive volumes track units rather than value. He also cites stagnating housing construction as one of the pressures on the sector. Points that may be worth considering include whether German furniture-sector exposure is tracked at the level of adhesive volume rather than customer revenue, and whether the kitchen and upholstery segments are forecast separately.

Handelsblatt | WirtschaftsWoche | Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung

item.title: US construction spending reached USD 2.158 trillion in July, down 3.8% from a year earlier and 0.5% from June, with demand for highways, data centres and power projects cushioning an otherwise soft picture.
item.description:
Commerce Department figures put the seasonally adjusted annual rate at USD 2,157.6 billion, a 0.5% decline from a revised June estimate. Private construction spending fell 0.5% and public spending 0.2%, so the weakness is not confined to one side. The contractors' association frames the year-on-year decline as occurring despite demand for new highways, data centres and power projects propping up the industry, which locates the strength in a narrow set of categories and the weakness across the rest.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Construction is among the larger end-markets for adhesive technologies, and a 3.8% annual decline in the value of US construction put in place is a demand signal that arrives before order books show it. The composition is the more useful part: with highways, data centres and power projects described as the categories holding the total up, the segments consuming the widest range of construction chemicals — commercial and residential building — are likely to be weaker than the headline. Data centre construction has a different material profile from conventional commercial building. Points that may be worth considering include whether US construction demand assumptions distinguish infrastructure and data-centre work from general building, and how far current volumes rest on the categories that reporting identifies as the exceptions.

Associated General Contractors of America | Dünya Gazetesi | MarketScreener

item.title: Germany's manufacturing PMI rose to 54.3 and Taiwan's to 62.5, its highest in almost five years, while India's fell to a five-year low of 52.8 and the UK's to a five-month low of 51.7; Russia fell into contraction at 48.8.
item.description:
Germany's reading, on the S&P Global final index, was driven by a third consecutive rise in new orders producing the strongest output growth in more than four and a half years, with firms citing defence spending, data centre build-outs and stockpiling; supplier delivery times lengthened and purchasing activity grew at its fastest since May 2022 as firms sought to secure inputs. Taiwan's index, from the Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research, rose a point to 62.5 with new orders at 66.5, but the same release flags rising costs and supply bottlenecks restricting orders and production schedules in electronics and optics, and customer inventories too low for a third month. India's HSBC index fell for a third consecutive month to 52.8, below its long-run average of 54.2, on slower output and new orders. The two US surveys differ: the ISM index fell a point to 54.6 with new orders down three points to 53.7, while S&P Global's US index was unchanged at 53.9. The euro-area index reached 52.7, a high since May 2022; Japan's rose to 54.9; Canada's slipped to 53.0 while still expanding for a fifth month; Russia fell to 48.8 from 50.7 with the fastest cost inflation since January, and Turkey rose to 48.1 from 47.7, still contracting.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The dispersion is the finding rather than any single number. Germany at 54.3 with input-securing behaviour and lengthening delivery times describes a market where availability, not demand, is becoming the constraint — the conditions in which supply agreements matter more than price lists. Taiwan at 62.5 with explicit supply bottlenecks says the same thing more sharply. India moving the other way, and doing so three months running, is the clearest divergence in the set. The ISM and S&P Global readings for the United States differ, which means the two surveys give different pictures of the same market in the same month. Points that may be worth considering include whether European and Taiwanese customers are signalling input-availability concerns that would justify earlier ordering, and which survey underpins current North American demand assumptions.

MarketScreener | Commercial Times | Commercial Times | Business Standard | The Hindu Business Line | MarketScreener | ISM | Interfax | Hürriyet Daily News | The Globe and Mail | Commercial Times

item.title: South Korea will impose anti-dumping duties of 8.32% to 19.17% on butyl acrylate imported from China from 28 September 2026 for five years; butyl acrylate is used mainly as a raw material for adhesives and special plastics.
item.description:
The measure was announced on 1 September and takes effect on 28 September for a five-year term. Chinese product accounts for 47% of the South Korean domestic market, which reporting puts at around KRW 100 billion as of 2024. The duty range is wide, from 8.32% to 19.17%, which normally indicates different rates for different exporters rather than a single sector-wide rate, though the allocation is not detailed in the reporting available. This is a trade-defence action on a specific chemical input rather than a general measure, and it takes effect in under four weeks.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Butyl acrylate is a direct feedstock for adhesives and special plastics, so this is one of the few measures in this alert that touches the input side rather than the demand side. The immediate effect is confined to South Korea, where roughly half the market has been supplied from China and where that supply carries an additional duty of 8.32% to 19.17% from 28 September. Whether the displaced volume is redirected to other markets, and whether comparable filings follow elsewhere, is not addressed in the reporting available. Points that may be worth considering include whether any Korean-market formulations depend on Chinese butyl acrylate at current landed cost, and whether comparable filings are pending in other importing markets.

Lianhe Zaobao

item.title: Three Chinese ministries issued guidelines urging automakers to avoid disorderly competition and disruptive pricing overseas, setting cost- and demand-based pricing as the permitted approach. No penalties for non-compliance are specified.
item.description:
The Ministry of Commerce, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the State Administration for Market Regulation issued the guidelines on 1 September. The 20 provisions cover antitrust compliance, intellectual property, data security, labour rights, quality management, overseas production safety, advertising, dealerships and pricing. On pricing specifically, companies are told to set clear price gradients between vehicle configurations, to take account of local market conditions, logistics costs and taxes when setting differences between countries, to mark prices clearly and not to charge unlisted fees, and not to disrupt competitive order in pursuit of an improper advantage. Component suppliers are covered alongside carmakers. One account notes the guidelines specify no punishments for non-compliance, which is a meaningful qualification on how binding they are. Separately reported: Geely, Chery, SAIC and BYD are expected to begin localising production capacity in the West in 2027, with Chery holding 40% of a joint venture at a former Nissan site in Barcelona targeting first-quarter 2027 production, SAIC seeking a plant in Galicia, FAW in talks with Stellantis about a Spanish plant, and Leapmotor planning two models in Spain.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Two things are moving at once and they point in opposite directions for European suppliers. Beijing discouraging price wars abroad would, if it holds, moderate the pricing pressure that Chinese entrants place on incumbent carmakers, which are customers for adhesive technologies. Against that, the localisation programme points to Chinese-brand assembly in Spain from 2027, with the reporting describing localisation in the West more generally, which creates supply opportunities in those plants while shifting volume away from existing ones. The guidelines specify no penalties for non-compliance, which distinguishes an intention from a constraint. Points that may be worth considering include whether qualification processes are positioned for Chinese-owned assembly plants in Europe, and how a change in Chinese pricing behaviour would flow through to established customers' own volumes.

China Daily | Xinhua | The Standard | MarketScreener | South China Morning Post | Lianhe Zaobao | Il Sole 24 Ore

item.title: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said no negotiations are taking place and that it is not clear Canada wants a deal, and that Washington is preparing to retaliate if Canada's counter-tariffs on about 700 US products take effect on 8 September.
item.description:
Greer said the response could include import bans or prohibitions comparable to Canadian measures. Reporting notes that most provinces have removed US alcohol from shelves and that some, including Manitoba, have changed rules to bar US companies from bidding on provincial contracts. Canada's counter-tariffs cover around 700 American products — valued at CAD 27.6 billion in one account and about USD 20 billion in another, described as matching the US duties dollar for dollar — at rates of 15% to 50%, including smartphones, cosmetics, kitchen appliances and some dairy items covered by the Canada-US-Mexico Agreement, with the hardest pressure on American steel and aluminium. Officials have told industry groups that the offer Canadian negotiators rejected on 21 August is now moot and that Washington is no longer willing to repeat its concessions on steel and aluminium, while Canada has drawn a line at US demands including a 25% tariff on medium and heavy trucks. Prime Minister Mark Carney said a mutually beneficial deal remains possible but that talks cannot resume while US officials publicly insult Canada; asked about the renaming of Lake Ontario as "Lake America" and other US comments denigrating the country, he said he walked away from a deal that asked too much and offered too little, over French-language discoverability on US streaming platforms and limits on Canada's freedom to sign trade agreements elsewhere. His party swept three by-elections held on Monday, winning Chicoutimi-Le Fjord ahead of the Bloc Québécois and the Conservatives and holding seats in Ontario and British Columbia. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer plans legislation to repeal the tariffs and require refunds. Reporting suggests the standoff may extend past the US midterm elections.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The change since last week is that both the negotiation and the de-escalation paths have narrowed: there are no talks, the previous US offer is described by officials as moot, and the US is preparing a further response to a Canadian measure that is six days away. Import bans, which Greer raised explicitly, work differently from tariffs for a manufacturer, because a prohibited good cannot be supplied at any price and re-routing takes longer than re-pricing. The product list matters for packaging and consumer-goods customers rather than for chemical inputs directly. Reporting reads the by-election sweep as evidence of a surge in support for Carney's position rather than as a change in the negotiating stance. Points that may be worth considering include which North American flows would be interrupted rather than merely taxed under a prohibition, and how long a re-route would take for the affected lines.

POLITICO | POLITICO | BNN Bloomberg | POLITICO | POLITICO | The Straits Times | BBC News | The Globe and Mail

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US is likely to announce Iran bank sanctions this week and again the week after, with airline leasing companies and entities that dealt with the Revolutionary Guard also under examination.
item.description:
This puts a timeline on a banking step that had not previously been dated; one account describes a single bank in each tranche, another refers to banks in the plural. Bessent described the aim as economically asphyxiating Iran's leadership after six months of conflict, said the effort is being coordinated with international allies and discussed with China; reporting notes a significant decline in Iran's currency. The European Union said it welcomes the US-led push and remains ready to take further measures, which Bessent presented as an early sign of success; several of the countries doing the most substantial remaining trade with Iran — China, Turkey, Iraq, Oman, Pakistan, India, Armenia and Azerbaijan — have said the least about their response. A separate strand of the campaign has already taken effect. The Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control indefinitely suspended education-related general licences permitting limited cooperation with Iran by American universities or individuals, after which the Educational Testing Service paused TOEFL and GRE examinations in Iran and Duolingo barred its English test for holders of Iranian identification. At the Bishkek summit, SCO leaders including Xi, Putin, Modi and Sharif signed a declaration condemning the US and Israeli war on Iran and Western sanctions on some of the organisation's members.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Bank designations reach further into commercial operations than entity listings, because they affect the settlement channels through which unrelated third-party trade moves rather than only the counterparties named. The unresolved question is whether large Chinese banks are included; Bessent's statement that the measures are being discussed with China does not settle it either way. Compliance exposure here is indirect and arises through customers, distributors and payment intermediaries in the region rather than through direct dealings. The education-licence suspension shows the campaign extending into activities with no evident military application, which is a guide to how broadly the remaining licences may be read. Points that may be worth considering include which banks in regional payment chains would need to be re-screened if designations land as described, and how quickly counterparty checks could be repeated at short notice.

The Economic Times | The Economic Times | Business Standard | Al Jazeera | POLITICO | Al Jazeera

item.title: Eurostat reported euro-area consumer prices up 3.3% year-on-year in August, from 2.9% in July and the highest since September 2023, driven by energy costs up 14.3%; economists quoted expect the European Central Bank to raise rates on 10 September.
item.description:
The increase of four tenths in a month is attributed to energy, with the energy component up 14.3% year-on-year, four percentage points more than in July, and the driver traced to the Middle East conflict. The reading is well above the ECB's 2% medium-term target and is the highest in more than three years. Spain is among the most affected, with a consumer price index of 4.5% against the euro-area average of 3.3%. Economists quoted in reporting expect the Governing Council to raise key rates at its 10 September decision, though that is an expectation held by economists rather than a decision, and the reporting available carries no ECB guidance either way. The euro-area manufacturing PMI reached 52.7 in August from 51.9, a high since May 2022, so the inflation print arrives alongside improving rather than deteriorating activity, though the reporting does not link the two.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

For European producers this reading is uncomfortable in a specific way: the inflation is coming from energy, which raises manufacturing costs directly, and the policy response to it would raise financing costs on top. That is different from demand-driven inflation, where higher prices at least accompany stronger orders. The dispersion between national rates — Spain at 4.5% against the 3.3% area average — means the pressure on customers and on wage negotiations will not be uniform across the European footprint. The manufacturing PMI at a four-year high suggests demand is not the constraint at present. Points that may be worth considering include how energy-cost assumptions for the fourth quarter are set against a possible further rise, and whether contracts with European customers have the flexibility to reflect input costs that are moving faster than the headline rate.

Süddeutsche Zeitung | La Vanguardia | Commercial Times

item.title: CME FedWatch put the probability of a 25 basis-point US rise in September at 68.2%, up from 39.6% a week earlier, and Governor Michael Barr said the Fed should be prepared to raise rates if inflation does not move convincingly towards 2%.
item.description:
The repricing has been rapid: from under 40% a week ago to more than two-thirds. Barr's intervention matters because it puts a sitting governor on record as open to a rise, conditional on the inflation data. He said price pressures could become increasingly difficult to contain after remaining above target for more than five years, that the economy is performing solidly on the back of AI investment and that the labour market is stable with relatively low unemployment. He also set out the other branch: if incoming data showed inflation moderating towards 2%, policymakers could afford to wait and assess, and that if progress stalls the Fed may need to respond more forcefully. The conditionality is explicit: he did not commit to a move. The 10-year Treasury yield reached about 4.79%, its highest since January 2025, on the same combination of renewed Middle East fighting and inflation concern; Brent was reported above USD 91 to 92 depending on the account. Separately, 1st Source Bank put US government debt above USD 40 trillion, around 122% of GDP against 119% at the end of the Second World War.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

A rise from a two-thirds probability is close to priced but not fully, so the residual market risk is concentrated in the event of the Fed not moving rather than moving. For companies with dollar debt or dollar-linked project finance, the more durable point is that a sitting governor has publicly tied the September outcome to the inflation prints, which makes the decision data-dependent rather than pre-committed. Barr's conditionality also matters: he tied the outcome to incoming inflation data, which means the September decision is still readable from the prints between now and the meeting rather than settled. Points that may be worth considering include whether financing decisions timed for the fourth quarter assume the current curve or a higher one, and how a stronger dollar arising from a US rise would interact with pricing in the export markets that matter most.

The Australian Financial Review | The Standard | LiveMint | NBC News | MarketScreener

item.title: Japanese government bonds sold off across the curve, taking the 10-year yield to 3.000%, its first visit to that level since October 1996, while finance minister Satsuki Katayama played down reports of US pressure on the Bank of Japan to raise rates.
item.description:
The move had three drivers according to reporting: expectations of another Bank of Japan rate rise, persistent concern about Japan's fiscal position, and renewed inflation worry after the resumption of US-Iran fighting pushed crude higher. The yen slid past 160 per dollar again. The diplomatic layer is the more unusual part. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said he hopes the Bank of Japan will raise rates, in comments one account frames as calling time on large-scale stimulus and as having effectively locked the bank into a September move. After meeting Governor Kazuo Ueda, the Treasury said Bessent called for good monetary policy to avoid excess exchange rate volatility, supported Japan's steps to address what he called significant yen undervaluation, and pointed to yen weakness as a contributor to Japanese inflation. Katayama's account was cooler: she said she and Bessent agreed that orderly yen movements are essential to global financial stability and confirmed their earlier joint currency intervention had been beneficial, but she played down the reports of pressure on the central bank. Markets price a September move as likely. Japan's manufacturing PMI meanwhile rose to 54.9 from 54.5, with new business growing at its fastest in more than eight years on demand for AI products and semiconductors.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

A 3% Japanese 10-year marks the end of the sub-3% long rate that has been a fixture of global fixed income for three decades. Two effects reach manufacturers. Japanese customers and competitors are financing against a benchmark that has not been at this level since 1996, while a yen strengthening from 160 would raise the cost of Japanese exports and lower the cost of imported inputs for Japanese producers. Tokyo's finance minister has played down press reports of US pressure on the central bank, while one account reads Bessent's comments as having effectively locked the bank into a September move; the two framings sit side by side in the reporting. Points that may be worth considering include how Japanese-market pricing and hedging assumptions hold if the yen moves sharply in either direction, and whether the strength in Japanese manufacturing orders is broad or concentrated in the AI and semiconductor chain.

The Mainichi | Bloomberg | Channel News Asia | The Mainichi | MarketScreener | Channel News Asia | MarketScreener

item.title: A G20 chair's statement closing the Asheville meeting recorded agreement by all participants except China that countries should end "non-market policies" worsening imbalances, and that those with excessive, persistent surpluses should lift demand curbs.
item.description:
A G20 chair's statement concluded the Asheville meeting. It says countries should eliminate non-market policies that exacerbate imbalances, and that countries with excessive and persistent external surpluses should remove distortions that constrain domestic consumption and produce an over-reliance on exports for growth. China's finance representative did not join. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went further in his own remarks, urging some of his counterparts to use tariffs and other measures against trade imbalances and saying the rest of the world probably needs to look hard at protecting its manufacturing base so that activity is not offshored; he recalled warning partners at the start of the administration that a US tariff wall would divert Chinese goods to their markets. Reporting indicates the administration is weighing an additional 7.5% tariff on Chinese imports following investigations into alleged Chinese excess industrial capacity and forced-labour regulations; it has not been imposed. Two other features of the meeting drew attention: the US invited Russia's finance minister Anton Siluanov for the first time in four years, which European delegations opposed, and Fed chair Kevin Warsh told the opening that the global economy has entered an "investment boom" driven by new projects and AI, leaving behind an era of surplus savings.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

A chair's statement is not a binding instrument and names no measures, so the immediate effect is political rather than legal. What changes is the level of cover: every G20 finance chief except China's has now put their name to language that treats surplus-driven trade patterns as a problem to be corrected, which lowers the diplomatic cost for any of them to act. For a manufacturer with production and customers on both sides, the risk is less a single large tariff than a widening set of national measures arriving at different times in different markets. The mooted 7.5% US tariff on Chinese goods remains under consideration rather than imposed. Points that may be worth considering include how many separate jurisdictions a given product line would need to be re-priced in if this language turns into measures, and whether current scenario planning distinguishes coordinated action from a sequence of national ones.

The Globe and Mail | The Standard | Al Jazeera | Japan Today | BNN Bloomberg | La Vanguardia | Chinatimes
